cases.title: `c.header()` crashes after consumption of the finalized res body
cases.body: `c.header()` crashes after consumption of the finalized res body. ### What version of Hono are you using? 4.13.13 ### What runtime/platform is your app running on? (with version if possible) Cloudflare Workers ### What steps can reproduce the bug? In a middleware, call the `c.header()` or a dependent such as `c.redirect()` or `setCookie()` after consumption of the **finalized** res body. ### What is the expected behavior? Always respond `"alternative response"` with a header `x-something: hey` successfully. ### What do you see instead? The most simple solution: user shall set, on his responsibility, `c.finalized = false` just after consumption of the res body. However, the `finalized` property, though public, seems to be undocumented officially at present. Resetting as `c.res = undefined` is pointless because `finalized` is still true. Another solution is to clear `c.finalized = false` when resetting as `c.res = undefined`. Since `set res` accepts `undefined` currently, this sounds semantically reasonable to me. cases.title: aws-lambda: a binary `+xml` response is corrupted (`application/vnd.apple.installer+xml`)
cases.body: aws-lambda: a binary `+xml` response is corrupted (`application/vnd.apple.installer+xml`). ### What version of Hono are you using? 4.13.8 (`main`, `098e1191`) ### What runtime/platform/OS are you using? `bun` 1.4.3 on macOS — the `aws-lambda` adapter, so this happens for anyone serving files from AWS Lambda (API Gateway, Function URLs or ALB). ### What steps can reproduce the bug? Return a file whose `Content-Type` ends in `+xml`, from an app running on AWS Lambda. `application/vnd.apple.installer+xml` is the media type of an Apple installer package. That file is **not XML** — it is a `xar` archive, so the first bytes are `xar!` (`78 61 72 21`) followed by binary integers and a compressed stream. The same happens with any media type that ends in `+xml` but holds a binary archive, for example `application/vnd.mozilla.xul+xml`. ### What is the expected behavior? The response body should be byte-for-byte identical to what the app returned. The adapter should treat this content type as binary and send it base64 encoded. ### What do you see instead? cases.title: fix(jsx/dom): execute previous ref cleanup when ref prop changes on re-render
cases.body: fix(jsx/dom): execute previous ref cleanup when ref prop changes on re-render. ### Problem Description In Hono's client-side JSX DOM renderer (`src/jsx/dom/render.ts`), when a DOM element's `ref` prop reference changes during a re-render (e.g., ` `), Hono registers the new ref callback `ref2(container)` and updates `refCleanupMap`, but it bypasses the cleanup function returned by the previous ref (`cleanup1` or `ref1(null)`). #### Root Cause Currently, `ref` cleanup is only triggered when a prop key is completely removed from the element via the deletion loop (`!(key in attributes)`). When a `ref` prop simply switches identity from `ref1` to `ref2`, `'ref'` remains in `attributes`, so the cleanup loop is bypassed. Consequently, any teardown logic attached to `ref1` (such as unbinding observers or cleaning up event listeners) is leaked and never executed. This leads to memory leaks in single-page applications when switching dynamic ref callbacks, conditional inline refs, or dynamic observers during component updates. --- ### Minimal Reproducible Example Add the following test case to `src/jsx/dom/index.test.tsx` and run `npx vitest run src/jsx/dom/index.test.tsx`: ```tsx it('execute

cases.title: Support custom Content-Type in compress middleware
cases.body: Support custom Content-Type in compress middleware. ### What is the feature you are proposing? I want to compress responses with `Content-Type: application/vnd.msgpack`. (FYI it's a MIME type registered with IANA: But Hono's compress middleware only compresses responses with known Content-Type defined here: I would like an option for custom conditions for which Content-Types are allowed to be compressed. However, I'm not sure what format the ideal option should take. (For example, a function that returns a boolean, a list of Content-Types, or a regex? Also, should it be possible to add or remove from a default list of Content-Types, or should all of them have to be specified manually?)

cases.title: CORS middleware allows origin: '*' with credentials: true
cases.body: CORS middleware allows origin: '*' with credentials: true. middleware/cors/index.ts sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true when configured with origin: '*' and credentials: true. The Fetch spec says Allow-Origin must not be * when credentials mode is include — browsers reject these responses. The middleware should either warn or reflect the request origin instead of *.

cases.title: Proposal to change to specifying `charset` parameter individually for each MIME type
cases.body: Proposal to change to specifying `charset` parameter individually for each MIME type. ### What is the feature you are proposing? Currently, MIME types parameter are set through mechanical determination. This has several problems. - There are other items besides `text/*` for which I want to specify a `charset` parameter (`image/svg+xml`, `application/xhtml+xml`, `application/xml`) - According to [IANA specifications]( not all `text/*` formats have a `charset` parameter Therefore, we will eliminate this processing and instead specify the `charset` parameter individually using the `_baseMimes` variable. (e.g. `css: 'text/css; charset=utf-8',`) Furthermore, in the `getExtension()` function, we will modify the logic to perform the check after removing the parameter instead.
